newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian children found with throats slit - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian children found with throats slit - paper.

text.p: Two child shepherds have been found with their throats slit in Bougara area, south of Algiers, the Algerian newspaper El Watan said on Thursday.
It said "terrorists", Algeria's term for Moslem fundamentalist rebels, had killed the children, both boys aged nine and 10.

The two had been tending their sheep on Bougara heights, some 20 km (12 miles) south of the capital. Their bodies were found on Tuesday, the paper said, adding that their killers had stolen the flock.
El Watan, giving its toll for a bomb blast in a cinema on Wednesday, in which the authorities said about 20 people were wounded, said one person had died, with 37 wounded.
Another newspaper, the Tribune, said the bomb, in a working class district of Algiers, had killed four people and wounded 30.

On Wednesday, the official Algerian news agency APS, quoted security forces as saying: "The bomb went off at around 1445 (local time) inside Le Musset Cinema in Belouizdad district...20 people were wounded including one in a serious state."

Late in May, at least five people were wounded when a bomb ripped through a cinema in Algiers. Seven people were killed by two bombs on buses in June and more than 40 were wounded on a train late last month.

The bombings prompted authorities to announce fresh security measures for the capital to try to thwart attacks they blamed on Moslem guerrillas. Officials at cinemas, trains, buses and other public places were ordered to carry out security checks on people and cars.
The Tribune newspaper said on Thursday: "The Musset bomb shows that security measures are not being applied in public places."
About 60,000 people have been killed in political violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
